title: Gatwick drop-off AutoPay breach, Nov 2026

subject.name: Gatwick Airport
subject.about: London Gatwick is an international airport in Crawley, West Sussex, about 30 miles south of central London. In 2024 it was the UK's second-busiest airport by passengers, after Heathrow.

disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by London Gatwick, Times24, ParkPark, any news outlet, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: One payment system for drop-off charges at one airport, though it is the UK's second-busiest. Gatwick has not said how many customers were affected. Flights, car parks and the drop-off zones themselves are working.
who_is_affected: People who registered for AutoPay to pay Gatwick's drop-off charge automatically; Gatwick says it has emailed those affected. Drivers can still use the drop-off zones and pay another way. Be wary of messages about parking, refunds or fines that ask for payment or bank details.

known.text: Gatwick says the company that runs its drop-off zones had unauthorised access to AutoPay, the system that charges drivers automatically.
Names, addresses, contact details, AutoPay logins and vehicle details were reached.
In a few cases payment records and partial card details (brand, last four digits, expiry date) were reached.
AutoPay has been switched off; flights, car parks and the drop-off zones are working.

not_known.text: When the access began and when it was found.
